Subject: NimbusHealth — Follow-up: reliability comparison, rate limits & next tests

Hi Eric / Nadia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a concrete test plan to validate reliability and failover behavior vs the hyperscaler baseline you mentioned. We focused on three evaluation buckets: uptime/SLA behavior, rate-limits & burst handling, and error-budget/failover behavior.

Summary of where Redwood sits compared to hyperscalers (high level):
- Uptime SLA: Redwood Hosted API (general) = 99.9%; Redwood Dedicated = 99.95% with SLA/credits.
- Rate limits: default hosted tier = 100 req/s per API key; Dedicated/Private configurable to high-throughput (we can provision 1k+ req/s with reserved capacity and autoscale policies).
- Failure policy: automatic model-variant fallback (when KV cache warmed) and regional fallback routing; we expose explicit failover telemetry and event hooks in the Console.
- Observability: token-level traces, per-route latency histograms, error budget burn charts and audit logs for Private.

Proposed tests (owners & rough timeline):
1) Controlled region failover (owner: Rafael) — Week of Oct 11
   - Simulate a us-east instance disruption and validate routing to us-west variant. Measure time-to-fallback and 95/99p latencies, target graceful degradation (no complete 100% error spike). Success criteria: rolling failover completed with <30s of elevated 5xx and application-level availability >99.9% during test window.
2) Sustained throughput with KV caching (owner: Logan) — Week of Oct 11
   - Run sustained traffic for 30m at your projected peak (tokens/min). Compare mean token cost and p95 latency vs hyperscaler. Include cold vs warm KV cache runs.
3) Error-budget burn test (owner: Soojin) — Oct 12
   - Introduce a 1–3% synthetic 5xx for 10 minutes and observe: automatic throttles, fallback triggers, and alerting cadence. Confirm consoles expose the exact error budget burn curve you can attach to your SRE playbook.
4) Burst / rate-limit profile (owner: Marissa) — Oct 13 (morning)
   - 10x burst for 30s; observe 429 behavior, queued requests, and retry guidance. Validate that Dedicated configs can be tuned to queue rather than drop for short bursts.

Deliverables we will provide before tests:
- Test harnesses (k6 scripts + sample workloads) and step-by-step runbook.
- A short SLO comparison matrix tailored to the NimbusHealth workload.
- Access to a sandbox Dedicated pool for the benchmark runs (no production data).

Attachments: nimbus_slo-action-plan.pdf (links into shared Drive) — I dropped a draft action plan and timeline in the Drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xb_example_drive_link

Next steps: please confirm the test owners above and whether Oct 11–13 works for your engineering team. If you prefer, Rafael can kick off the smoke tests earlier in a small pilot window.

Thanks — looking forward to proving the failover characteristics you care about.

--

Thanks Soojin — this is great. A couple clarifying items before we lock the windows: 

- On the region failover success criteria: can you share the exact latency bands you plan to capture (p50/p95/p99) and the definition of "elevated 5xx" you used? Our SRE will need the thresholds to map to our on-call runbook.
- For error-budget burn: we want the test harness and the exact failure injection method (HTTP 500 at the edge vs model-serving layer). Please include the k6 script and the ramp profile.
- Data residency / logs: if we run the Dedicated sandbox, will audit logs include request-level metadata (IP, timestamp, API key) for each test? We need those to reconcile against our internal monitoring.

We are definitely interested in the pilot — Oct 11–13 should work but I need to confirm with our SRE for the exact windows. Rafael, could you include the k6 harness and your recommended request shapes?

On the SLA: 30s of elevated 5xx sounds optimistic — happy to validate but we also need to compare measured user-visible errors (our downstream service returns 200 with partial payloads in some hyperscaler outages) — if you have an example of the console traces for a prior failover that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Eric

Thanks — adding configuration detail for the benchmark runs. I can own the failover test and run the smoke pilot in our sandbox. Notes below and attached checklist (slo-test-checklist.md).

Benchmark configuration suggestions:
- Redwood model variant: rwd-7b-quant (int8) with kv-cache enabled for warm runs.
- Hyperscaler baseline: hsc-7b-standard (as discussed) with default autoscale.
- Batching: continuous batching enabled; target batch size 32, max latency target 150ms for p95.
- Token lengths: run three profiles: short (prompt 32 tokens -> completion 64), medium (128->256), long (512->1024).
- Failure injection: prefer injecting 500s at the model-serving layer for one test and at the network edge for another — we’ll provide both k6 harness variants.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a temporary Dedicated sandbox key scoped to the test traffic and logging enabled to include API key, timestamp, and region. Audit logs will be accessible via the Console and we can export a CSV for your team.
- For the failover run: plan for a 10-minute warm-up, a 5-minute outage injection window, then 20-minute recovery and observation.

I attached the checklist: slo-test-checklist.md. I'll spin up the sandbox tomorrow and post access details to the Drive.

-Rafael
